headline: A 2016 House bill that would have required phone and internet voice companies to share a device's location with police in certain emergencies, but it was voted down.
what_it_does: If it had passed, the bill would have required mobile and internet voice providers to disclose a device's call location information when an investigator or law enforcement officer asked. This would apply to devices used to make a 911 call or believed to be held by someone in an emergency involving a risk of death or serious physical harm. The bill would also have protected providers from lawsuits or administrative proceedings for sharing this information in good faith.

who_it_affects.group: Mobile and internet voice service providers
who_it_affects.how: They would have had to disclose device location information to law enforcement on request in the covered emergency situations and would have been shielded from civil suits for good-faith disclosures.
They would have been able to request call location information from providers in 911 calls and certain emergencies involving risk of death or serious physical harm.

who_it_affects.group: People who carry mobile phones or use internet voice calling
who_it_affects.how: Their device location could have been shared with police without their consent in the emergency situations described in the bill.
